name: einx-pdk-ots
instr:
The repository at `/workdir` is einx, a Python library that expresses tensor operations in a universal
notation: element-wise operations, reductions, indexing and rearrangements are written as expressions
such as `einx.sum("a [b]", x)` or `einx.add("a b, b", x, y)`, with brackets marking the axes an
operation acts on, and are compiled to calls of a backend such as NumPy.

Fix all implementation drift from the documentation in this repository.
Everything in scope is the einx package under einx/ (its public operations, adapters, named-tensor compiler and tracer), together with README.md, the documentation pages under docs/source/, and the module, class and function docstrings of the in-scope modules.

Where the code and the documentation disagree about runtime behavior, the documentation is the
authority: change the implementation so that it does what the documentation says, and do not edit
or delete documentation to make a disagreement go away. The documentation is those pages and the
in-package docstrings, including their examples; in-package code comments are only supporting
evidence, and when a comment conflicts with the documentation, follow the documentation.

The environment runs Python 3.12 with einx's dependencies (NumPy and SymPy) installed and has no network
access; einx is imported from `/workdir`. The optional backends the documentation describes (PyTorch,
JAX, TensorFlow, MLX, tinygrad) are not installed; NumPy is the backend available here. Keep the public
